title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in Massachusetts's 7th Congressional District
description: The 2026 election for Massachusetts's 7th Congressional District pits four-term incumbent Democrat Ayanna Pressley, a member of the progressive 'Squad,' against independent candidate Kelechi Linardon. The district encompasses roughly three-fourths of Boston, as well as parts of Cambridge and Somerville, and is one of the most reliably Democratic districts in the country with a Cook PVI of D+34. Pressley, first elected in 2018 after defeating incumbent Michael Capuano in the Democratic primary, is seeking a fifth term after declining to challenge Senator Ed Markey in the 2026 Senate primary. The Democratic primary is scheduled for September 1, 2026; additional general election candidates may emerge following the primary.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found specifically for this race as of mid-2026. The district is rated 'Solid D' by The Cook Political Report.

candidates.name: Ayanna Pressley
candidates.summary: Ayanna Pressley is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. She is a member of the progressive 'Squad' in Congress and previously served on the Boston City Council. Pressley announced in December 2025 that she would seek reelection rather than challenge Senator Ed Markey in the 2026 Democratic primary.

candidates.summary: Kelechi Linardon is an independent candidate running for U.S. House to represent Massachusetts's 7th Congressional District. Linardon declared candidacy for the 2026 election and is listed on Ballotpedia as a general election candidate. Additional biographical details were not available from authoritative sources at the time of research.

forecast.rationale: No public district-specific polls are available, limiting confidence from direct survey evidence. However, district fundamentals are overwhelmingly Democratic: MA-07 has a Cook PVI of D+34, one of the highest Democratic lean scores in the country, and is rated 'Solid D' by Cook. Incumbent Ayanna Pressley is a four-term Democratic representative and a well-known figure in the district. The only currently listed general-election opponent is Kelechi Linardon, an independent candidate with very limited public profile, no campaign website, and no donor or career history available. A Democratic primary is scheduled for September 1, 2026, after which additional general election candidates could emerge, but no Republican or other major-party challenger has filed to date. Based on present field strength and district fundamentals, Democrats hold an overwhelming advantage consistent with a safe rating.
